text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Urgent MRI of the brain with and without gadolinium, with diffusion imaging and MR angiography of the head and neck, within three days; EEG within a week; ECG, blood count, metabolic panel, calcium, and TSH today; headache and episode diary
  • Safety now: no driving until the cause is known and her seizures are controlled for the period her state requires; showers rather than baths, no swimming alone, and no work at heights; seizure first aid explained; come at once for a longer episode, weakness that does not recover, or a severe sudden headache
  • Neurosurgery consultation if the MRI shows a structural lesion, to explain the options and their risks to her and plan treatment with her
  • Grief and mood: a grief history, PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at each visit, and the neuro-oncology counselor offered; no assumption that her symptoms are "nerves"
  • Protect her writing: occupational therapy assessment of hand function if weakness persists, and voice dictation as a backup
  • Levetiracetam 500 mg twice a day for focal epilepsy due to the meningioma; seizure diary; ask about irritability and low mood at each visit; continue for at least a year after surgery, then decide with her whether to taper after an EEG
  • Shared decision: resection by craniotomy aiming at Simpson grade I, her choice after observation (not advised for a symptomatic tumor with edema and seizures) and stereotactic radiosurgery (less suitable at 3.1 cm with edema next to the motor cortex) were explained; dexamethasone 4 mg twice a day from three days before surgery, tapered and stopped after it; MRI within 48 hours after surgery
  • After resection of a CNS WHO grade 1 meningioma (Simpson grade I): no radiation; MRI at three months and then yearly for five years, then every two years; no progestin-containing hormone therapy without discussion

resource.title: Mary Shelley synthetic care plan
resource.description: Evaluate headaches with transient numbness and weakness of one side in a 51-year-old writer: distinguish focal seizures from transient ischemic attack and migraine aura, obtain MRI with gadolinium and an EEG, and give driving and seizure-safety advice at once. Confirm a left convexity meningioma over the motor cortex with vasogenic edema and focal epilepsy; start levetiracetam and monitor mood and irritability; use dexamethasone only for symptomatic edema and briefly; present observation, resection, and stereotactic radiosurgery by shared decision-making (EANO 2021 and NCCN); grade the tumor by the WHO CNS5 criteria after resection, decide on adjuvant treatment by grade and extent of resection, and set the surveillance MRI schedule. Throughout, take a grief history and screen for depression in a woman with many early losses, and protect her ability to write. The teaching note contrasts this with the supposed tumour of the left hemisphere on her death certificate and the hemiplegic migraine hypothesis.
